_comment: The controlled relationship vocabulary, plus hand labels for boards that
shipped before agents recorded a `shape` per pair.
Replaced the homegrown 13-shape free-text list on 2026-08-04 (design.md
D-3): that list sampled ~3 of the taxonomy's 10 families, and with the
field uncontrolled, 40% of authored pairs were uncountable by the variety
brief. Every shape here is a relation type from Bejar/Chaffin/Embretson
(1991) via SemEval-2012 Task 2 (docs/research/semeval-2012-taxonomy.md),
carrying three levels:
family — the taxonomy family (1-10). Library-coverage axis: the variety
brief steers toward underused families over time.
stance — the felt kind of question a set asks. Board-composition axis:
a board wants four different stances (the arrow finding, D-3).
Derived from Herrmann & Chaffin's relation elements (1984),
recorded per entry in `elements` for audit.
shape  — the entry's own id. Measurement axis: what a pair declares.
`symmetric: true` marks a shape whose A-to-B relation IS its B-to-A
relation, so a player cannot tell which way round the author wrote it
(design.md D-9, 2026-08-06). The engine accepts a pair flip only when BOTH
pairs flip together, so a symmetric set asks the player to guess an
orientation and then mirror it — and charges a mistake for guessing wrong.
Two of the four entries already said so in their own failureMode before the
field existed. It is a REPORTING flag, never a blocklist: a symmetric shape
whose words carry a convention (north before south) is perfectly fair, and
saying which is 06's job, not this file's.
Selection rule for the list itself: B must be a THING — noun, agent,
event, action or abstraction, never an adjective. Adjective-shaped types
(5a, 6a, 'Gulf Stream : warm') are absent by construction; this is what
enforces retired rule-007's real intent. Families 5 and 6 are excluded
entirely: their thing-shaped types contribute only stances already covered
three other ways, and their vocabulary runs against rules 004/012.
`failureMode` is what the review card shows Max so his checklist widens
with the output space: each kind of relation, taught beside its example.
`portableStances` are the five stances reachable from four or more
families; the composition rule counts only these as required, since
`reference` reaches exactly one family and `dimension` three.
Counts are NOT stored here — studio/variety.js recomputes them on demand
from what shipped and what runs produced, so there is no second mutable
file to drift out of step with the runs themselves.

stances.description: A names a kind or group; B is one of it, or equal to it
A has, holds or wears B — no time in it
The relation is what A lacks or falls short of — the question runs against the board's grain
A and B sit on one scale — nearer and further, or opposed
Someone or something acts: who does it, on what, with what
A brings B about — makes, produces, enables or prevents it
A stands for, plans, depicts or hides B
A and B are stages or moments in one unfolding order

shapes.description: A category and a kind of thing within it
shapes.failureMode: fails when B is an instance, not a kind — 'flower : this rose' names one flower, not a type of flower

shapes.description: A kind of thing and one of them by name
shapes.failureMode: fails when the named individual is obscure — the challenge must be spotting the membership, not knowing the name

shapes.description: A collection and the kind of thing it is made of
shapes.failureMode: fails when the collection has mixed contents — a drawer holds many things, a forest is made of trees

shapes.description: A thing and a feature it simply has — no time in it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the feature is not distinctive — every surface has edges; only some wear craters

shapes.description: A thing and the stuff it is made of
shapes.failureMode: fails when it collapses into material-becomes-object read backwards — 'glacier : ice' is composition, 'ice : glacier' is a different (cause) claim

shapes.description: A creature and the thing that belongs to it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the belonging is occasional — a robin without a nest is still a robin in spring

shapes.description: The one thing it can never have
shapes.failureMode: fails when the absence isn't distinctive — everything lacks most things; a shadow lacking weight is the point of shadows

shapes.description: A moment or feature and the larger activity it belongs to
shapes.failureMode: fails when the part could belong to many activities — a whistle starts many games; a kickoff starts one

shapes.description: A stage and the whole it opens, closes or belongs to in order
shapes.failureMode: fails as a progression chain when a middle term repeats (rule: four distinct words) — 'second : minute :: minute : hour' is illegal

shapes.description: Two names for the same thing
shapes.failureMode: fails when the two words differ in register or shade — near-synonyms make the order feel arbitrary
shapes.symmetricNote: car : auto reads the same as auto : car — naming one thing twice is mutual

shapes.description: The same kind of thing, smaller then larger on one scale
shapes.failureMode: fails when the scale is fuzzy — both words must clearly sit on one dimension, in one order

shapes.description: One thing becomes another through a process
shapes.failureMode: fails when the becoming is occasional, not necessary (rule-011) — a caterpillar reliably becomes a butterfly; a student only sometimes becomes a professor

shapes.description: Two counterparts of the same kind, side by side
shapes.failureMode: fails when the pairing has no axis — ram/ewe differ by sex; two random sheep differ by nothing nameable
shapes.symmetricNote: ram : ewe reads the same as ewe : ram — counterparts side by side have no from/to

shapes.description: An action and the action that undoes or answers it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the reversal is loose — 'attack : retreat' answers differently than 'attack : defend'; pick one axis and hold it

shapes.description: Two ends of one spatial axis
shapes.failureMode: fails when the two orders read the same — the pair must not be reversible without changing the claim
shapes.symmetricNote: front : back reads the same as back : front — an axis has two ends, not a start

shapes.description: A flawed form and the faculty it falls short of
shapes.failureMode: fails when it reads as mere opposite — a limp is not the opposite of walking, it is walking with something missing

shapes.description: Two moments facing each other across one span
shapes.failureMode: fails when the span is unclear — dawn and dusk bracket a day; two random hours bracket nothing

shapes.description: A worker and the thing their work is about
shapes.failureMode: fails when B is the worker's product read as cause — 'tailor : suit' is what the work is about; if the reveal says 'makes', it has drifted to cause

shapes.description: One who acts and the one acted for
shapes.failureMode: fails when the roles blur — mentor : protege holds; friend : friend has no direction

shapes.description: A worker and the tool of their trade
shapes.failureMode: fails when the tool is generic — many workers use trucks; the tool must belong to this trade

shapes.description: A thing and the instrument made for working it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the instrument is shared — a violin has its bow the way a nutmeg has its grater; a knife cuts everything

shapes.description: A role and the object that marks it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the marker drifts to symbol — 'king : crown' is worn possession; 'scepter : authority' is reference, a different question

shapes.description: Something that acts and the result it produces
shapes.failureMode: fails when B only sometimes follows A (rule-011) — 'telescope : discovery' breaks; 'foul : free throw' holds

shapes.description: The thing that lets another thing do what it does
shapes.failureMode: fails when the enabling is generic — electricity enables everything; a match is for lighting

shapes.description: A tool and the action it exists to perform
shapes.failureMode: fails when B is one of many uses — a brush paints, sweeps and scrubs; the action must be the tool's purpose

shapes.description: The thing that stops another thing
shapes.failureMode: fails when prevention is partial — an umbrella slows rain reaching you; an antidote defeats the poison

shapes.description: A place and the thing kept there
shapes.failureMode: fails when the location is incidental — books live on bookshelves; keys are merely sometimes on tables

shapes.description: A place and what it exists to produce
shapes.failureMode: fails when the place merely contains rather than produces — a bakery makes bread; a pantry only holds it

shapes.description: A place and the activity it exists for
shapes.failureMode: fails when the activity happens everywhere — learning happens anywhere, but school is FOR it; hold the 'exists for' reading

shapes.description: Two things defined by touching — where one ends, the other begins
shapes.failureMode: fails when the border is incidental — a coast is DEFINED by meeting the ocean; two adjacent fields just happen to touch
shapes.symmetricNote: coast : ocean reads the same as ocean : coast — touching is mutual by definition

shapes.description: A thing and where it fastens
shapes.failureMode: fails when the attachment is loose — a belt is made for a waist; a bag merely hangs from many shoulders

shapes.description: A season or moment and what belongs to it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the timing is loose — harvest belongs to summer's end; errands belong to no season

shapes.description: A signal and what it announces
shapes.failureMode: fails when the sign is private — a siren means danger to everyone; a knotted handkerchief means something to one person

shapes.description: A thing and its made image
shapes.failureMode: fails on order drift — 'person : portrait' and 'portrait : person' are different claims; hold one direction across both pairs

shapes.description: The written form of a thing and the thing itself
shapes.failureMode: fails when it drifts to cause — a recipe DESCRIBES the cake; an oven MAKES it. If the reveal says 'produces', it is in the wrong stance

shapes.description: A cover and the true thing beneath it
shapes.failureMode: fails when the hiding is figurative — an alias hides a name by design; a smile 'hiding' sadness is a metaphor, not a mechanism
